text: Floor and wall tiling across London. Victorian path restorations, hallways, kitchens and bathrooms, laid by hand and finished properly.

title: How Kieron works
text: Kieron lays the patterned floors London's Victorian and Edwardian houses were built with: front paths, porches, hallways and balconies. Every floor is set out by hand, tile by tile, so the borders run true and the pattern meets the walls the way it should.

Most jobs start with a visit. Kieron looks at the space, checks what's underneath, talks through patterns and colours with you, and gives you a clear quote. If there's an old floor worth saving, he'll say so.
From preparing the base to cutting, laying, grouting and sealing, the whole floor is done properly, so it's ready for the next hundred years of muddy boots.

title: Pattern library
text: Choose from the classic Victorian geometric patterns: chequerboards, stars, diamonds and rosettes, framed with a border. Kieron brings samples on the visit and helps you pick colours that suit the house and the street.

title: Copy existing pattern
text: Cracked or missing tiles replaced with ones that match, or an original pattern carried on into a new space, like a hallway floor continued out onto the front step. The aim is that nobody can tell where the old floor ends.

title: New pattern
text: A design made for your space: your own mix of shapes and colours, a border that follows a curved bay, or a pattern worked around an awkward corner. Kieron draws it up with you before a single tile is laid.
